raw_application_ranking.text: I have carried this apology in my coat for four days without posting it. Every evening I tell myself the post office has already shut. There is a slot in its door. We both know that, which makes the excuse particularly poor.

raw_application_ranking.text: The envelopes addressed to fourteen Salt Lane keep coming back because the house was demolished in June. Its residents moved before the demolition, but no forwarding address was lodged with this office. The red RETURN TO SENDER mark is our ordinary hand stamp.

raw_application_ranking.text: The ferry made no crossing during the storm. Its hull was tied alongside the repair slip from nine in the evening until the following afternoon. Any account of a passenger being carried across that night requires a boat other than ours.

raw_application_ranking.text: Elsie, I told the harbour committee that you had misplaced the mooring ledger. That was not true. I left it on the ferry bench, and the tide took it when the boat flooded. I let you carry the blame because I was afraid of losing my berth.

raw_application_ranking.text: No train left Morrow Quay at eleven forty on the night of 18 October. Floodwater had covered the cutting beyond Bracken Bridge. I cancelled the departure at ten fifty and chained the platform gate. The locomotive remained in its shed until morning.

raw_application_ranking.text: The revolving mechanism stopped shortly after eleven. Its brass drive pin had sheared, leaving the beam pointed towards the open sea instead of sweeping the quay. raw_application_ranking.text: There is a postcard from my sister in the biscuit tin. Please leave it there until I return. I have not decided whether to join her inland. A person may think about leaving for a long time without having made a plan.

raw_application_ranking.author: Ada Venn, instrument repairer

raw_application_ranking.text: Somebody has mistaken the stamp’s broken R for a second message. There is no hidden word in it. The rubber split last winter, and the council has not approved its replacement. I can show you the stamp beside the sorting tray.

raw_application_ranking.text: The station clock was seventeen minutes slow when I examined it on the morning of 19 October. Damp had swollen the wooden case against the pendulum. I dried the case and set the hands from the observatory signal at noon.

raw_application_ranking.text: I intend to cross by the south causeway after calling at the station. The tide table on the chandlery wall is from last year, so I cannot trust it. If the water is too high, I shall turn back. Do not wait up with the oven lit.

raw_application_ranking.author: Ada Venn, instrument repairer

raw_application_ranking.text: Mara, I am taking the recorder to the old signal house tonight. The canvas case has a split handle, so I have tied it with cord. If the late train is running, I will ask the porter to send my tools inland tomorrow.

raw_application_ranking.author: Ada Venn, instrument repairer

raw_application_ranking.text: The voice saying “come home before the dark” was on a wax cylinder, not arriving over the wireless. A loose contact started the dictation machine whenever the building’s door slammed. I disconnected that contact on Tuesday and the repeated voice stopped.

raw_application_ranking.text: I have left the cylinder with the headteacher rather than scrape it clean. The last few seconds contain laughter and a chair falling over. Those ordinary sounds seem worth keeping, even if the words at the beginning have frightened half the street.

raw_application_ranking.text: The lighthouse drive pin can be made here, but I need the broken piece to copy its diameter. Silas’s order asks for brass rather than iron because salt air eats the cheaper metal. I have put the material aside and am waiting for the sample.
raw_application_ranking.title: Seventeen minutes
raw_application_ranking.author: Arthur Fenwick, clock repairer

raw_application_ranking.text: At eleven twenty on 18 October I was watching North Point from my sewing-room window. The lighthouse lantern was completely dark; not merely turned away, but dark behind every pane I could see. I wrote the time on a scrap before closing the shutters.

raw_application_ranking.text: I used the mantel clock, not the station clock, to mark the hour. Whether it was keeping good time that evening I cannot swear. The storm shook soot from the chimney and I had other things to attend to than the hands of a clock.

raw_application_ranking.text: When you wound that little toy, its beak opened before a sound came out. We used to wait for the missing note and then whistle it ourselves. I have kept it because nobody else would understand why a broken bird was worth saving.

raw_application_ranking.author: Nora Finch, seamstress

answer.text: The sound heard along the harbour was our stationary engine. Porter Bell released its pressure twice while checking the boiler. A whistle in the fog is not evidence of a departure. The passenger ledger contains six names; all six were refunded at the booking window.

I have left the cylinder with the headteacher rather than scrape it clean. The last few seconds contain laughter and a chair falling over. Those ordinary sounds seem worth keeping, even if the words at the beginning have frightened half the street.

The voice saying “come home before the dark” was on a wax cylinder, not arriving over the wireless. A loose contact started the dictation machine whenever the building’s door slammed. I disconnected that contact on Tuesday and the repeated voice stopped.
